assessment: Current culture-based, gold standard methods used for diagnosing the cause of sepsis provide results in 48-96 hours slowing antibiotic treatment initiation and leading to poor patient recovery. This work provides a new tool for identifying sepsis- and pneumonia-causing pathogens in less than 4 hours with species-specificity with the hope that the fast turnaround time leads to early treatment and improved clinical outcomes. Using an optimized PCR+CRISPR-Cas12a DNA detection method, the assay demonstrates good analytical sensitivity and specificity for 10 common bacterial pathogens that cause pneumonia. The method is validated in a clinical cohort and the clinical benefit is analyzed using a second cohort which is an intervention study used to guide clinicians on treatment choice.
